one_liner: Discord has a broad REST API with self-serve OAuth2 apps and bot tokens, free to register; only community MCP servers found.
auth_notes: Authorization-code OAuth2 with self-serve app registration covers user-scoped access. Bot tokens are also supported. Basic auth (client_id:client_secret) applies only to the OAuth2 token endpoints.
access_notes: Anyone can register a developer application and get a client ID/secret or bot token. Privileged intents can be toggled on in the Developer Portal below 10,000 users; review is needed above that. Some scopes are partner-only. The pages do not state pricing explicitly, but no paid plan is mentioned.
blocker_notes: No blocker for building. Privileged intent review applies only at scale (over 10,000 users), and partner-only scopes exist but are not needed for the core API.

evidence.quote: We support the authorization code grant, the implicit grant, client credentials, and some modified special-for-Discord flows for Bots and Webhooks.
Using a bot token found on the Bot page within your app’s settings.
Using an OAuth2 bearer token gained through the [OAuth2 API](/developers/topics/oauth2).
The first step in implementing OAuth2 is [registering a developer application](https://discord.com/developers/applications) and retrieving your client ID and client secret.
If your app has fewer than 10,000 users, you may access Privileged Intents by enabling them in the Developer Portal.
You can use the [Discord OpenAPI Spec](https://github.com/discord/discord-api-spec) to generate a client in your preferred backend language
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that provides Discord integration capabilities to MCP clients like Claude Desktop.
